description: A seed.apply (or seed.restore) on a connection the daemon cannot attribute to a peer refuses with the seed's no-actor code (S43-extra T6, the -31832): the actor comes from the connection (the daemon's ActorFor seam), never from params, and an unresolvable or empty peer id is refused rather than stamped with a placeholder (SD10). The honest absence (a storeless daemon has no persons) is the refusal, not a default — an unattributed seed is a silent no-op the audit cannot name, and the three-part data says so without the handler filling in anything (this is the one seed refusal that carries the registry's own sentence, not the engine's).

error.message: no actor for a seed write

data.what: the seed write needs a person, and this connection named none
